Scheduler Fuzz & Resilience Lab Manual

Overview:

This lab manual documents the Scheduler Fuzz & Resilience Lab: the curated experiments, deterministic replay tooling, profiling practices, benchmark handoffs, and the operational runbook used by serving-runtime engineers to validate scheduler and kernel changes before canary and prod rollout. The lab targets regressions that are difficult to catch in unit tests and classical microbenchmarks, including priority inversion, eviction oscillation, NVLink-induced preemption stalls, and non-deterministic warmup losses.

Goals:
- Provide reproducible test recipes that catch subtle QoS and cross-tenant fairness regressions.
- Integrate fuzzed adversarial campaigns with deterministic replay for CI gating.
- Produce artifacts consumable by the benchmarking pipeline and release gates.

Lab topology and components:
- det-replay (deterministic replay harness): replays NDJSON trace records against a latency model and scheduler policy. Produces event-trace.log, per-tenant latency CSV, and kernel-usage CSV.
- sched-fuzzer: creates mutated traffic mixes and scheduler-parameter perturbations. Supports random, grid, and boundary sweep modes.
- prof-orchestrator: manages profiler agents, sampling windows, and full-trace collection on selected worker pools.
- chaos-injector: simulates node-level perturbations (thermal throttling, NVLink degradation, short network egress saturation).

Signals and artifacts produced (examples):
- event-trace.log (canonical, used for exact-replay checks)
- operational-signature.json (normalized SLO deltas and fairness metrics)
- kvcache-hit.csv (per-tenant cache hit ratios over time)
- kernel-calls.csv (callsite latency histogram)

Trace format (NDJSON example):
{"req_id":"r-0001","tenant":"t-acme","seq_len":64,"priority":"P1","arrival_ms":0}
{"req_id":"r-0002","tenant":"t-beta","seq_len":1024,"priority":"P3","arrival_ms":5}

Deterministic replay configuration snippet (YAML as string):
kernel_latency_profiles: small: {base_ms: 0.45, per_token_ms: 0.025} large: {base_ms: 2.0, per_token_ms: 0.075}
scheduler_policy: path/to/policy.json

Recommended experiment recipes:
1) Short-high vs long-low priority inversion sweep
- Setup: 80% long low-priority (seq_len >= 768), 20% short high-priority (seq_len <= 64) across 5 tenants.
- Run: sched-fuzzer --mode grid --param priority_ratio --values 0.01,0.05,0.1,0.2 --trace mixed-corpus.ndjson --out out/priority-sweep
- Instrumentation: prof-orchestrator annotate --full-trace on two worker nodes; enable scheduler decision debug logs.
- Acceptance: P1 median < 35ms, P95 < 140ms, preemption delay occurrences < 1 per 10k requests.

2) Eviction warmup boundary test
- Purpose: ensure model swap preserves prefix locality and prevents long-term cache thrashing.
- Steps: warm with N representative prefixes (N sweep: 1k, 10k, 50k), perform model rollout, replay warm set and measure hit ratio trajectory for first 30 minutes.
- Acceptance: hit ratio drop <= 6% after swap and rolling median latency <= 1.6x baseline within 5 minutes.

3) Admission-storm replay + NVLink perturbation
- Setup: 10x burst for 30s injected at t=0 while chaos-injector triggers a transient NVLink degradation for 5s at t=10s.
- Objective: reveal preemption stalls and kernel retry patterns.

Fuzz campaign modes and parameters:
- random (seeded) campaign: repeatability via seed stamping in metadata. Always record seed in event-trace.log.
- grid sweep: exhaustively vary one or two parameters (priority_ratio, slice_ms, preempt_window_ms).
- boundary sweep: test edge conditions (very small batches, extreme priority ratios).

CI and benchmark integration:
- CI job should run a short det-replay suite (canonical 12 scenarios) and 20 quick fuzz mutations as a fast pre-gate. Artifacts to persist: operational-signature.json, event-trace.log, kvcache-hit.csv.
- For a full merge validation (nightly): run sched-fuzzer campaign=200, run prof-orchestrator sampling on 3 nodes, upload artifacts to s3://lab-artifacts/scheduler-fuzz/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/.
- Bench mapping: operational-signature.json feeds the bench dashboard and is retained 90d; event-trace.log retained 180d for replay equality checks.

Release readiness checklist (kernel/scheduler change):
1) Unit tests and static analysis pass.
2) Deterministic replay: new policy passes canonical scenarios with no P99 regressions >20% relative to baseline.
3) Fuzz campaigns: no SEV-HIGH regressions across 200 mutation runs.
4) Profiling: primary kernel call latency mean change < 10%.
5) Bench: end-to-end throughput within tolerance defined in SLO matrix.
6) Canary: 1% traffic, 24h baseline monitoring, incremental ramp with automated rollback on SLO violation.

Severity taxonomy (lab):
- SEV-HIGH: P99 increase > 30% or cross-tenant fairness delta > 25%.
- SEV-MED: P95 increase 15-30% or sustained kvcache hit drop 6-15% for > 10m.
- SEV-LOW: transient deviations that resolve within 10m or small hit ratio drops < 6%.

Runbook: quick triage steps
1) Alert sources: CI gate failure, staging shadow mismatch, canary SLO alert.
2) First 10 min: fetch operational-signature.json from artifacts, compare to baseline using lab-tools bench-compare.
3) If repro exists in lab: run sched-fuzzer reproduce --id  --seed  --out replay/. If not reproducible, run det-replay with same seed and record mismatch.
4) Containment: rollback canary or revert scheduler preset via Admin API: POST $ADMIN/scheduler/preset/rollback with target stable tag.
5) Deep analysis: run prof-orchestrator collect --full-trace --annotate replay/event-trace.log and examine kernel-calls.csv for increased tail at specific callsites.

Known issues observed and mitigations (lab-tracked):
- NVLink transient stalls can trigger preemption retry loops. Mitigation: on NVLink error signals, scheduler applies exponential backoff for preemption and routes heavy long-running allocations away from degraded links.
- Replay inequality due to unrecorded seed metadata. Mitigation: stamp seed into event-trace.log header and validate replay equality in CI.

Metrics and dashboards to monitor:
- lab.sched_fuzz.campaign_count (counter)
- lab.det_replay.success_rate (gauge)
- lab.kvcache.hit_ratio (per-tenant time-series)
- lab.kernel.call_mean_ms (histogram)
Dashboards: Grafana IDs lab-sched-fuzz, lab-det-replay, lab-kernel-latency.

Operational ownership:
- Lab owner: Aisha Kumar (serving-runtime)
- Scheduler reviewer: Liam O'Connor
- Profiling automation: Sofia Martinez
- SRE escalation: Daniel Park

Appendix: sample quick commands
- Run a short deterministic check:
  det-replay run --scenarios canonical/* --out out/det
- Launch a seeded fuzz campaign:
  sched-fuzzer run --campaign 50 --trace samples/mixed-corpus.ndjson --seed 20260315 --out out/fuzz
- Reproduce a failing campaign:
  sched-fuzzer reproduce --campaign-id 1234 --seed 20260315 --out out/replay/1234

Artifact retention guidance:
- operational-signature.json: 90 days
- event-trace.log: 180 days
- kernel-calls.csv: 365 days

Change log:
- 2026-02-10: initial draft published by Aisha Kumar.
- 2026-03-15: added CI patterns, severity taxonomy, and expanded NVLink mitigation notes.

Contact and contribution:
Open issues and experiment requests: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-lab/issues. For rapid coordination, ping #serving-runtime-lab on Slack or message Aisha.K.
